claims: The Masters Green Jacket has been awarded since 1949 to the Masters champion.
The Masters Green Jacket has been worn by Augusta National members since 1937 to identify them to patrons.
The Masters Green Jacket is an "Augusta Green" (Pantone 342C) wool blazer featuring an embroidered left-breast patch.
Masters Green Jacket winners may take the jacket home for one year before returning it to be stored on-site.
Masters Green Jacket winners return their jackets to the clubhouse 12 months after their victory.
Masters Green Jacket winners' jackets are stored in a designated cloakroom.
Masters Green Jacket winners' jackets are worn only while on the premises.
If a Masters Green Jacket winner wins again, they do not get a new jacket unless a new fit is needed.
Only a first-time and reigning Masters champion may remove his Green Jacket from the Augusta National club grounds.
The Masters Green Jacket was inspired by red jackets worn by captains at Royal Liverpool.
Co-founder Bobby Jones brought the Green Jacket concept to Augusta.
The first Green Jackets were introduced in 1937 to differentiate members from patrons.
The Masters Green Jacket is made of lightweight wool.
The Masters Green Jacket is a single-breasted blazer.
The Masters Green Jacket features brass buttons with the PGA logo.
Rory McIlroy won the 2026 Masters.
Rory McIlroy's 2026 Masters win marked a consecutive win.
Rory McIlroy's 2026 Masters win was his second Green Jacket.
Hideki Matsuyama won the Masters in 2021.
Hideki Matsuyama never had his Green Jacket dry cleaned for the entire first year that he was allowed to keep it.
